open1.text: This is a simulated benchmark, in its third round: two alloy discovery campaigns, replayed for a whole year in a digital twin of our planned automated lab. This cut compares the two labs like for like.
open1.spoken: This is a simulated benchmark, in its third round: two alloy discovery campaigns, replayed for a whole year in a digital twin of our planned automated lab. This cut compares the two labs like for like.
open1.phonemes: ðɪs ɪz ɐ sˈɪmjʊlˌeɪɾᵻd bˈɛntʃmɑːɹk, ɪn ɪts θˈɜːd ɹˈaʊnd: tˈuː ˈælɔɪ dɪskˈʌvɚɹi kæmpˈeɪnz, ɹˈiːpleɪd fɚɹə hˈoʊl jˈɪɹ ɪn ɐ dˈɪdʒɪɾəl twˈɪn ʌv ˌaʊɚ plˈænd ˈɔːɾəmˌeɪɾᵻd lˈæb. ðɪs kˈʌt kəmpˈɛɹz ðə tˈuː lˈæbz lˈaɪk fɔːɹ lˈaɪk.

open2.text: Some of it comes from real sources: the lab's design and its 3-D model, footage from our own atomizer, the search spaces in the two proposals, and published prices. Everything else is simulated: every alloy, every measurement, and every result.
open2.spoken: Some of it comes from real sources: the lab's design and its three D model, footage from our own atomizer, the search spaces in the two proposals, and published prices. Everything else is simulated: every alloy, every measurement, and every result.

chg1.text: Round three removes the cap on how much work is in flight. What sets the pace now is physical: stations, robots, people and fixtures. Decisions come every simulated hour, one spending plan paces the money for every policy, and the thirty-day immersion gives interim readings and can be stopped early.

dag1.text: Each campaign is a function network: a chain of steps, where each step's results feed the next. BOFN, Bayesian optimization over function networks, models every step, not just the final score.
dag1.spoken: Each campaign is a function network: a chain of steps, where each step's results feed the next. B O F N, Bayesian optimization over function networks, models every step, not just the final score.

dag2.text: For aluminium, the lab makes each alloy's powder itself, then prints it and checks every build.
dag2.spoken: For aluminum, the lab makes each alloy's powder itself, then prints it and checks every build.

dag3.text: For copper, a one-hour corrosion screen ranks the DED deposits, and thirty days in seawater come before a utility is known.

fig1.text: Best so far is the highest utility of any new alloy tested yet. The first dotted line is the best existing alloy on this synthetic benchmark. One random design in twelve beats it, so it is a low bar.

fig3.text: The grey dashed curve is a conventional lab run by rule of thumb, through partner and core facilities. Here both labs order their metal as they go: the comparison is like for like.

fig4.text: Days to a target are the median over twelve runs. Here the automated lab reaches the halfway target on day 183, in 11 of its 12 runs. The conventional lab does on day 337, in only 6 of 12, so its median is its last run to get there. The factor is therefore a lower bound: at least 1.8 times.

cu1.text: Day 221. In seed five, copper's best new alloy passes the best existing alloy on this synthetic benchmark.

res1.text: Twelve simulated one-year runs per policy in the automated lab. On aluminium, time-aware BOFN and pKGFN finished highest, at 0.73 and 0.71. On copper, tiered CALPHAD screening still finished ahead, at 0.69 against 0.58 and 0.61.

res1.phonemes: twˈɛlv sˈɪmjʊlˌeɪɾᵻd wˈʌnjˈɪɹ ɹˈʌnz pɜː pˈɑːlɪsi ɪnðɪ ˈɔːɾəmˌeɪɾᵻd lˈæb. ˌɔn ɐlˈuːmɪnəm, tˈaɪmɐwˈɛɹ bˈiː ˈoʊ ˈɛf ˈɛn ænd pˈiː kˈeɪ dʒˈiː ˈɛf ˈɛn fˈɪnɪʃt hˈaɪɪst, æt zˈiəɹoʊ pɔɪnt sˈɛvən θɹˈiː ænd zˈiəɹoʊ pɔɪnt sˈɛvən wˈʌn. ˌɔn kˈɑːpɚ, tˈɪɹd kˈælfæd skɹˈiːnɪŋ stˈɪl fˈɪnɪʃt ɐhˈɛd, æt zˈiəɹoʊ pɔɪnt sˈɪks nˈaɪn ɐɡˈɛnst zˈiəɹoʊ pɔɪnt fˈaɪv ˈeɪt ænd zˈiəɹoʊ pɔɪnt sˈɪks wˈʌn.

res2.text: Days to each target, with every run a mark. Time-aware BOFN and pKGFN reach aluminium's halfway target on day 96 and day 83, in 11 and 10 of 12 runs. BOFN per dollar does in 7, and no other policy in more than 2. The heuristic reaches the first target soonest, on day 24, and then stalls. On copper, tiered screening reaches the halfway target on day 148, in 10 of 12 runs.

res2.phonemes: dˈeɪz tʊ ˈiːtʃ tˈɑːɹɡɪt, wɪð ˈɛvɹi ɹˈʌn ɐ mˈɑːɹk. tˈaɪmɐwˈɛɹ bˈiː ˈoʊ ˈɛf ˈɛn ænd pˈiː kˈeɪ dʒˈiː ˈɛf ˈɛn ɹˈiːtʃ ɐlˈuːmɪnəmz hˈæfweɪ tˈɑːɹɡɪt ˌɔn dˈeɪ nˈaɪnti sˈɪks ænd dˈeɪ ˈeɪɾi θɹˈiː, ɪn ɪlˈɛvən ænd tˈɛn ʌv twˈɛlv ɹˈʌnz. bˈiː ˈoʊ ˈɛf ˈɛn pɜː dˈɑːlɚ dˈʌz ɪn sˈɛvən, ænd nˈoʊ ˈʌðɚ pˈɑːlɪsi ɪn mˈɔːɹ ðɐn tˈuː. ðə hjuːɹˈɪstɪk ɹˈiːtʃᵻz ðə fˈɜːst tˈɑːɹɡɪt sˈuːnɪst, ˌɔn dˈeɪ twˈɛnti fˈɔːɹ, ænd ðˈɛn stˈɔːlz. ˌɔn kˈɑːpɚ, tˈɪɹd skɹˈiːnɪŋ ɹˈiːtʃᵻz ðə hˈæfweɪ tˈɑːɹɡɪt ˌɔn dˈeɪ wˈʌnhˈʌndɹɪd fˈɔːɹɾi ˈeɪt, ɪn tˈɛn ʌv twˈɛlv ɹˈʌnz.

res3.text: Removing the cap did not speed copper up: money is its limit. More than four fifths of each campaign's spending is orders of metal and consumables. With three times the copper money, BOFN and pKGFN gain 0.14 and 0.08 over four runs each, and draw level with tiered screening, which is still first to both targets.

res3.phonemes: ɹᵻmˈuːvɪŋ ðə kˈæp dɪdnˌɑːt spˈiːd kˈɑːpɚɹ ˈʌp: mˈʌni ɪz ɪts lˈɪmɪt. mˈɔːɹ ðɐn fˈɔːɹ fˈɪfθs ʌv ˈiːtʃ kæmpˈeɪnz spˈɛndɪŋ ɪz ˈɔːɹdɚz ʌv mˈɛɾəl ænd kənsˈuːməbəlz. wɪð θɹˈiː tˈaɪmz ðə kˈɑːpɚ mˈʌni, bˈiː ˈoʊ ˈɛf ˈɛn ænd pˈiː kˈeɪ dʒˈiː ˈɛf ˈɛn ɡˈeɪn zˈiəɹoʊ pɔɪnt wˈʌn fˈɔːɹ ænd zˈiəɹoʊ pɔɪnt zˈiəɹoʊ ˈeɪt ˌoʊvɚ fˈɔːɹ ɹˈʌnz ˈiːtʃ, ænd dɹˈɔː lˈɛvəl wɪð tˈɪɹd skɹˈiːnɪŋ, wˌɪtʃ ɪz stˈɪl fˈɜːst tə bˈoʊθ tˈɑːɹɡɪts.

lfl1.text: Now the two labs, like for like: both order their metal as they go. To aluminium's halfway target, BOFN and pKGFN in the automated lab are at least 1.8 times sooner than a conventional lab run by rule of thumb. They got there in 11 of 12 runs, against 6 of 12, so this is a lower bound. To copper's halfway target, with tiered screening in both labs, the automated lab is 3.2 times sooner, with an interval from 1.9 to 4.8.

lfl1.phonemes: nˈaʊ ðə tˈuː lˈæbz, lˈaɪk fɔːɹ lˈaɪk: bˈoʊθ ˈɔːɹdɚ ðɛɹ mˈɛɾəl æz ðeɪ ɡˈoʊ. tʊ ɐlˈuːmɪnəmz hˈæfweɪ tˈɑːɹɡɪt, bˈiː ˈoʊ ˈɛf ˈɛn ænd pˈiː kˈeɪ dʒˈiː ˈɛf ˈɛn ɪnðɪ ˈɔːɾəmˌeɪɾᵻd lˈæb ɑːɹ æt lˈiːst wˈʌn pɔɪnt ˈeɪt tˈaɪmz sˈuːnɚ ðˌænə kənvˈɛnʃənəl lˈæb ɹˈʌn baɪ ɹˈuːl ʌv θˈʌm. ðeɪ ɡɑːt ðɛɹ ɪn ɪlˈɛvən ʌv twˈɛlv ɹˈʌnz, ɐɡˈɛnst sˈɪks ʌv twˈɛlv, sˌoʊ ðɪs ɪz ɐ lˈoʊɚ bˈaʊnd. tə kˈɑːpɚz hˈæfweɪ tˈɑːɹɡɪt, wɪð tˈɪɹd skɹˈiːnɪŋ ɪn bˈoʊθ lˈæbz, ðɪ ˈɔːɾəmˌeɪɾᵻd lˈæb ɪz θɹˈiː pɔɪnt tˈuː tˈaɪmz sˈuːnɚ, wɪð ɐn ˈɪntɚvəl fɹʌm wˈʌn pɔɪnt nˈaɪn tə fˈɔːɹ pɔɪnt ˈeɪt.

stk1.text: Stocking is its own effect, and it is not the lab's. In the automated lab, having the metal on the shelf brings BOFN and pKGFN to aluminium's halfway target 1.9 and 2.2 times sooner than ordering as they go. Round three's 4.0 times was that stock multiplied by the lab's 1.8.

stk1.phonemes: stˈɑːkɪŋ ɪz ɪts ˈoʊn ɪfˈɛkt, ænd ɪɾ ɪz nˌɑːt ðə lˈæbz. ɪnðɪ ˈɔːɾəmˌeɪɾᵻd lˈæb, hˌævɪŋ ðə mˈɛɾəl ɔnðə ʃˈɛlf bɹˈɪŋz bˈiː ˈoʊ ˈɛf ˈɛn ænd pˈiː kˈeɪ dʒˈiː ˈɛf ˈɛn tʊ ɐlˈuːmɪnəmz hˈæfweɪ tˈɑːɹɡɪt wˈʌn pɔɪnt nˈaɪn ænd tˈuː pɔɪnt tˈuː tˈaɪmz sˈuːnɚ ðɐn ˈɔːɹdɚɹɪŋ æz ðeɪ ɡˈoʊ. ɹˈaʊnd θɹˈiːz fˈɔːɹ pɔɪnt zˈiəɹoʊ tˈaɪmz wʌz ðæt stˈɑːk mˌʌltɪplˈaɪd baɪ ðə lˈæbz wˈʌn pɔɪnt ˈeɪt.

tie1.text: Where the automated lab does not win. Against the same optimizer in a conventional lab, with both ordering as they go, it is about a tie on aluminium's halfway target: 0.9 times for BOFN and 1.0 for pKGFN, on four seeds. And in those seeds the conventional lab, with three years and three years' money, reached copper's best existing alloy more often.

cost1.text: Cost, on one basis: what a campaign had spent when it reached the target. With both labs ordering as they go, the automated lab spent at least 2.2 times less to aluminium's halfway target than the lab run by rule of thumb, and 3.2 times less to copper's, with tiered screening in both. Against the same optimizer, it spent about the same, or more. This basis leaves out fixed costs: staff, equipment and the building, where round three found the automated lab costs more.

note1.text: Everything here is simulated: the alloys, the results, and every measurement, with modelled noise not yet calibrated on the lab's instruments. The atomizer's rates, station times and fees, the stock on the shelf and the spending plan are assumptions. It shows how a lab design and its policies interact in a model, not what the real lab will find.
